newsitem.title: UK: EIB jumbo lira Eurobond to have structured coupon.
newsitem.headline: EIB jumbo lira Eurobond to have structured coupon.

text.p: The European Investment Bank's proposed jumbo lire-into-euro Eurobond may carry some form of structured coupon to avoid having to launch the deal as a discounted issue, sources close to the deal said on Friday.
"The coupon structure will be slightly different (to the other EIB euro-fungible bonds which carry a 5.75 percent coupon)," a syndicate manager said.

Primary market sources said this could be in the form of some additional payment to bondholders in the first year or two of the deal's life to boost the yield, given the level of long-term Italian rates.

Earlier, the EIB awarded the mandate Banca Nazionale del Lavoro, Credito Italiano and Paribas the mandate to jointly lead manage a 1.0 trillion lire Eurobond due February 15, 2007, with launch next week.
When Italy adopts the euro the proposed lira deal will be redenominated into euros by the EIB.
It will then be fungible with the EIB's four outstanding 5.75 percent Eurobonds denominated in escudos, French francs, guilders and marks, which all carry 5.75 percent coupons.

However, giving the EIB lira deal just the same 5.75 percent coupon would mean having to price the deal at a chunky discount to par. This, in turn, would leave Italian investors with a taxable capital gain.

The third stage of European economic and monetary union, including the introduction of the European Union's planned single currency, the euro, is prescribed by EU law to take place no later than January 1, 1999.
